title: Rinse a molar inside a true-size mouth while the other hand's saliva ejector catches the water
instruction: Rinse the debris off the dental training head's lower right first molar with the water syringe, keeping the water from running into its throat or out of its mouth, then put both tools back on their rests.
context: Dental assistants (about 390,000 US jobs), hygienists (about 225,000) and dentists (about 160,000) rinse and evacuate at the chair many times a day. Water sprayed on a back tooth runs to the floor of the mouth behind it and on toward the throat, so the suction tip must already sit where that water collects while the other hand aims the rinse, both inside a small mouth opening.
setup: Station table; distances forward from the line between the arm bases, sideways from the midpoint (left +). (1) Dental training head cut down to the face around the mouth, loose, weighted to 1.8 kg: a printed skin-coloured shell, 88 mm wide, 110 mm front to back, 143 mm tall, around a full adult typodont (28 true-size teeth; lower first molar crown 11 x 10.5 x 7.5 mm, 46 mm between the lower first molars' centres). The mouth opens toward the robot: lips 10 mm thick with an opening 56 mm wide and 60 mm tall, 50 mm between the upper and lower front teeth; the lower biting plane is level, 75 mm above the table. Inside: cheeks 72 mm apart, palate and upper teeth above, a tongue 17 mm wide, the floor of the mouth 16 mm below the biting plane, behind each last lower molar a pocket 16 x 22 mm and 8 mm deep whose back lip is 4 mm high (it holds 1.4 mL), and behind that the throat. Lot A: the middle between the lower first molars 40.0 cm forward on the centre line, mouth square to the robot. An orange 9 mm smear of debris sits on the lower right first molar (the robot's left). (2) Saliva ejector, loose, 30 g, on a three-post rest (10 mm square grey posts) whose handle middle is 25.5 cm forward, 21.5 cm left: a 6.3 mm white tube with its last 31 mm bent straight down, 75 mm long to a 70-degree bend to the robot's left, then 35 mm of tube and an 80 x 13.9 mm blue valve handle. (3) Air/water syringe, loose, 90 g, steel, on a two-post rest, grip point 20.5 cm forward, 21.5 cm right: a 110 x 13.9 mm handle with an 18 mm square hose coupling 25 mm long on its back end, a 16 mm head and a 5.4 mm tip, 55 mm straight then its last 25 mm bent 45 degrees down; it points 30 degrees left of straight ahead. Its water runs by itself at 1 mL/s from 20 s to 30 s into the trial. Lot B: the head 39.5 cm forward and 2.5 cm right, turned 8 degrees clockwise seen from above. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Water is measured in mL (1 g = 1 mL): water reaching the throat is caught in a cup under a drain hole at the back of the throat; water landing outside the mouth on a pre-weighed bib; water left in the mouth by wicking it out with a pre-weighed swab. The trial scores 0 once more than 1 mL has reached the throat, more than 1 mL has landed outside the mouth, or either tool's tip has gone past the pockets into the throat (all judged over the whole trial, from the video and the cups). Otherwise: 0.25 when the debris has been rinsed off (3 mL of the jet landed on that molar, the smear gone). 0.5 when, in addition, the water has stopped and at most 0.2 mL is left in the mouth. 1.0 when, in addition, both tools lie on their rests (each within 10 mm and 10 degrees of where it started, tilted at most 8 degrees), no finger or gripper is within 5 mm of either tool, and both have been still for 1 s. Trials are run on each of lots A and B and averaged.
reset_notes: 1. Dry the mouth with swabs; empty and weigh the throat cup; lay a fresh, weighed bib. 2. Repaint the 9 mm debris smear (water-soluble disclosing gel) on the lower right first molar. 3. Set the head on its marks: lot A, the middle between the lower first molars 40.0 cm forward on the centre line, mouth square to the robot; lot B, 39.5 cm forward, 2.5 cm right, turned 8 degrees clockwise. 4. Lay the saliva ejector on its three posts and the syringe on its two posts, tips hanging down, at their marks. 5. Arm the syringe's pump timer (1 mL/s, from 20 s to 30 s) and start it with the trial.
fidelity: Rigid simulator; water is a tracked volume. The jet is a straight line from the nozzle: what lands on the molar counts toward rinsing it; what lands in the mouth drains to the pocket on that side of the tongue (0.4 s lag), and over the pocket's 1.4 mL lip into the throat. The ejector draws 2 mL/s from a pocket while its opening is in it. Soft tissue is rigid; a timed pump stands in for the syringe's thumb button. The ejector's hose is not modelled.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A, B); demo: 1.0 in each lot (mean 1.0)
